438009996|StatusCurrent state Under DiscussionDiscussion thread https lists apache org thread njjznyly38td4scb9bjc8v0gq7kc1yqjJIRA here Change the link from KAFKA 1 to your own ticket MotivationThe long standing problem silent data loss on partition expansionIncreasing a topic s partition count is a routine operational task not an exceptional event Topics are often created with a moderate number of partitions to balance cost and resource utilization then expanded as workloads grow When a topic is expanded a consumer configured with auto offset reset latest can silently miss every record produced to the newly added partitions before the consumer becomes aware of them The sequence is straightforward The topic is expanded and the new partitions immediately begin receiving records The consumer does not learn about the new partitions until its next metadata refresh or assignment update This creates a short metadata blindness window When the consumer is assigned the new partitions no committed offsets exist for them As a result auto offset reset applies Under latest the consumer seeks to the log end offset and skips all records produced during the blindness window The loss is completely silent the consumer never observes the skipped records and no error warning or metric indicates that data was lost This remains one of the most common surprises associated with the latest reset policy Why previous proposals stalledTwo earlier KIPs attempted to address this issue by introducing new protocol level mechanisms Both ultimately became difficult to move forward because of their semantic and operational complexity KIP 1282 proposed a new reset policy to start time which anchors resets to the consumer group s creation timestamp While this is an elegant fit for partition expansion the proposal did not reach consensus on offset out of range behavior Under that design a consumer whose committed offset is out of range would reset to earliest while a consumer whose group metadata had been garbage collected would reset to latest Reviewers considered this behavior difficult to reason about and inconsistent with the principle that backlog should be treated uniformly KIP 1327 proposed an auxiliary configuration auto offset reset new partitions together with a group creation time based classifier that distinguishes newly added partitions from existing ones Implementing this requires persisting group creation timestamps modifying on disk record formats such as ConsumerGroupMetadataValue and PartitionRecord adding new metadata version and group version gates and extending GroupHeartbeatResponse with a NewPartitions field The proposal also raised follow on questions around share groups and mirrored clusters Taken together these changes introduce substantial protocol and operational complexity to address what is usually a very small timing window Late in the KIP 1327 discussion reviewers converged on a simpler observation a by duration value in the 5 10 second range already covers the common partition expansion case given the default heartbeat interval ms of 3 seconds The residual reprocessing introduced by such a policy is also of the same order of magnitude as the small backlog that latest already tolerates between fetching the end offset and beginning consumption This KIP adopts that approach The key insight a small replay window is safer than silent data lossFor an actively running consumer the interval between partition creation and consumer discovery is bounded by the heartbeat and assignment cadence of the group protocol Under default settings this interval is typically only a few seconds 5 seconds for the modern consumer group s group consumer heartbeat interval ms and 3 seconds for the legacy heartbeat interval ms This is the only period during which silent loss can occur for an actively running consumer KIP 1106 already provides a mechanism that naturally covers this window by duration The policy resolves a reset position using a timestamp based ListOffsets lookup at now duration For a partition created only seconds earlier no records exist before that timestamp so the lookup naturally resolves to the beginning of the partition and no records are lost For a pre existing partition assigned to a consumer without a committed offset only the most recent few seconds of records are replayed This makes a small duration default both practical and safe latest already tolerates a small amount of backlog The latest policy is not a perfect zero backlog policy It inherently allows a small amount of backlog to accumulate between fetching the end offset and actually beginning consumption Records produced during that gap are consumed after the reset A bounded five second replay window is of the same order of magnitude The safer failure mode is bounded replay With latest records can be silently and permanently skipped With by duration PT5S the worst case outcome is a bounded re read of a few seconds of recent data Re reading a small amount of recent data is generally harmless and self correcting silently skipping live data is not Why this proposal does not attempt to solve extended downtimeA recurring question in earlier discussions was how reset semantics should behave when a consumer is offline for an extended period while partitions are added This proposal does not attempt to special case that scenario Losing records produced to newly added partitions during an extended downtime is consistent with the semantics of latest If a consumer is offline for a long period and a new partition is created during that downtime a user who selected latest typically expects the consumer to resume from the current tail not from the beginning of the new partition solely because the partition is technically new to the group A user who selects latest has already accepted that backlog accumulated during downtime may be skipped on any partition Newly added partitions are not fundamentally different from existing partitions in this respect Attempting to distinguish quot briefly unaware of a partition quot from quot offline for a week quot introduces timing dependent behavior that is difficult to explain and reason about It also reintroduces the same protocol complexity that KIP 1282 and KIP 1327 attempted to manage by duration PT5S provides a clear and consistent boundary It protects consumers from the short blindness window during which they had no opportunity to observe newly added partitions while preserving the user s intent to ignore older backlog The quot backlog is backlog quot principleThe central observation is that historical data and live data differ only in the amount of backlog involved Rather than introducing new reset policies or partition classifiers users should have a single consistent way to express how much backlog they are willing to tolerate when a reset occurs by duration already provides that abstraction Changing the default from latest to a small non zero duration transforms one of Kafka s most surprising default behaviors silently losing live data after partition expansion into a predictable and bounded behavior replaying at most a few seconds of recent records This achieves the desired outcome without introducing any new public APIs RPCs metadata records or version gated protocol changes GoalsEliminate silent data loss during partition expansion for the common case of actively running consumers using the modern consumer group protocol Apply the same safe default consistently to the modern consumer and the share consumer Kafka Streams is out of scope for this change because it already overrides the source consumer reset policy to earliest through StreamsConfig CONSUMER DEFAULT OVERRIDES Non goalsThis KIP does not attempt to change behavior for consumers that remain offline long enough to accumulate substantial backlog Skipping such backlog is consistent with the intended semantics of latest This KIP does not than commenting on the wiki wiki discussions get unwieldy fast MotivationThe ZooKeeper to KRaft migration is designed so that a cluster can linger in the dual write phase and roll back to ZooKeeper mode if an operator discovers a problem before the migration is finalized In production environments at any point in time hardware failures may happen some of which are cause for replacing nodes such as failing disks Kafka fully supports node replacements out of the box These two aspects node replacements provisioning and KRaft migration rollback are documented as orthogonal concepts However it has been observed in production systems that node replacements during a KRaft migration when following the documented procedures breaks the ability to roll back This is not documented and as both mechanisms are important tooling for operators to keep clusters available it s preferable to make them work in conjunction There is no way to eliminate the risk of hardware failures during an ongoing migration and as such the sanctioned tooling needs to be adapted to handle them Today when a broker is lost during the migration and the documented process for provisioning a replacement is followed the replacement s storage is formatted using the kafka storage sh format procedure That command unconditionally writes meta properties with version 1 If a rollback is later required the operator configures the brokers back into migration mode at which point the newly provisioned broker rejects its own storage and crashes before becoming available CDATA java lang RuntimeException Found unexpected version in srv kafka meta properties ZK based brokers that are not migrating only support version 0 which is implicit when the version field is missing at org apache kafka metadata properties MetaPropertiesEnsemble verify MetaPropertiesEnsemble java 489 at kafka server KafkaServer startup KafkaServer scala 258 The incompatibility is not documented and node replacement is a routine operation for managed fleet operators The result is a silent loss of the rollback capability that the migration is supposed to preserve discovered only at the worst possible time during an attempted rollback The broker itself already formats empty log directories with a rollback compatible version 0 meta properties when it starts up in migration mode so the capability exists in the code base It is simply not reachable through the provisioning tool that operators are instructed to use This KIP closes that gap Public InterfacesA new optional flag is added to the format subcommand of takes no argument When it is passed the format command performs storage formatting identically to how the broker itself does during a migration sequence resulting in a meta properties with version 0 phases section links to it The documentation makes clear that the flag is only relevant while a migration can still be rolled back and should no longer be used once the migration has been finalized Compatibility Deprecation and Migration PlanThe change is fully backward compatible The flag is opt in and omitting it preserves the current behavior byte for byte No configuration no other command line option and no on disk default is altered for existing users There is nothing to deprecate and no migration required Operators who are not performing a ZooKeeper to KRaft migration have no reason to use the flag and are unaffected Test PlanUnit tests assert both directions of the behavior at both layers that were changed The storage tool verifies that format zk rollback compatible produces a broker and is cheap to expose

does not cleanly apply Many members could send their heartbeat requests any of which can trigger a new assignment causing partition add revoke on the consumer A lagging member adopts the latest target assignment and skips the intermediate state changes between epochs from the last heartbeat Therefore a single coordinator reason does not fit the real quot cause quot of a rebalance for that particular member To let the consumer client calculate the intermediate states we return a bit mask of each state from the last member epoch to the current group epoch We only include the reasons in a heartbeat response when the member indeed needs a new assignment which is the real trigger for a rebalance to be triggered on the client anyway CoordinatorEach protocol resolves the cause at its epoch unwieldy fast MotivationKafka Connect s Single Message Transform SMT framework allows users to build chains of transformations that process records between the connector and Kafka Transforms can modify records route them to different topics or drop them entirely by returning null a filter operation When combined with the error tolerance framework errors tolerance all records can also be diverted to a Dead Letter Queue DLQ before reaching the connector Today the transform layer has two significant gaps no operational observability and no mechanism for sink connectors to learn about records they never received This KIP addresses both with two complementary enhancements Problem 1 No Per Transform Operational MetricsKafka Connect provides no operational metrics at the transform layer The existing connector transform metrics group only exposes static metadata Existing MetricTypeDescriptiontransform classGauge string The class name of the transformationtransform versionGauge string The version of the transformationThis creates several operational pain points No visibility into filtering When using the Filter transform or any transform that drops records by returning null operators have no way to know how many records are being filtered The only workaround is subtracting task level source record poll total from source record write total or sink record read total from sink record send total which provides only an aggregate across the entire transform chain No per transform throughput In a chain of 3 5 transforms operators cannot determine the throughput contribution or bottleneck of each individual transform If a transform has a bug that silently drops records it goes undetected No error attribution While task error metrics tracks aggregate errors operators cannot determine which transform in a chain is causing failures without correlating with debug level logs Capacity planning gap Without per transform record counts operators cannot make informed decisions about whether a transform is cost effective e g quot is this filter dropping 90 of records or 1 quot The consumer group protocol and other Kafka subsystems have rich per component metrics The transform layer is a notable gap Problem 2 Offset Gap for Sink Connectors When Records Are SkippedThe SinkTask preCommit API allows sink connectors to control which offsets are committed to Kafka Many production connectors override this method to implement exactly once or at least once delivery guarantees with external systems These connectors track offsets based on records they receive in put and only return offsets from preCommit after durably writing to the external system When transforms or error tolerance drop records before put these connectors have no visibility into the dropped records The result Offset gap The consumer position advances past the dropped records but the sink s committed offset does not include them Reprocessing after rebalance On rebalance the consumer seeks to the last committed offset and re fetches the dropped records The transforms drop them again and the cycle repeats Infinite reprocessing loop If all records for a partition are dropped the sink returns an empty map from preCommit the framework skips commit entirely and no progress is ever made for that partition This problem affects widely used connectors in production ConnectorOffset StrategyImpactS3 SinkReturns offsets only after flushing to S3 rotation interval record count Filtered records create offset gaps Rebalance reprocesses all records since last S3 flushIcebergSinkConnectorWorkers commit offset only after coordinator signalTrailing filtered records never committed Gap grows with each poll cycleAny connector using preCommit returning Full offset opt outIf all records filtered partition offset permanently frozenHow the Two Problems RelateThe two problems form a diagnose fix pair CDATA Per Transform Metrics Part A Skipped Record Notification Part B DIAGNOSE Which transform is FIX The sink can now track offsets dropping records and how many for records it never received Operator sees transform record Connector overrides onRecordSkipped filtered total climbing on to incorporate skipped offsets into filterNull transform at 632 sec its preCommit return value Together they close the loop Without Part A operators cannot diagnose where records are being dropped Without Part B connectors cannot act on records they never received Together they provide complete observability and correctness for the transform pipeline The use of SMTs and Predicates in production has grown significantly since their introduction Common patterns that trigger these problems Filter SMT Drop records not matching criteria e g filter by record type tenant region RegexRouter Predicate Route and filter based on contenterrors tolerance all Tolerate conversion errors send to DLQHeaderFilter Predicate Drop records missing required headersMulti tenant pipelines Filter per tenant records across shared topicsSuccess CriteriaAreaCriterionObservabilityOperators can query per transform record in record out and record filtered counts via JMXObservabilityOperators can compute per transform filter rates for alerting and dashboardsCorrectnessSink connectors that override preCommit can track offsets for all consumed records including three complementary enhancements to Kafka Connect s transform pipeline Part A Per Transform Operational Metrics Six new JMX metrics per transform stage records in records out records filtered as AlternativesAlternative 1 Framework Offset FloorApproach The framework tracks skipped record offsets internally and enforces a minimum quot floor quot offset during commitOffsets Even when the sink returns custom offsets from preCommit the framework would advance the committed offset to at least the skipped record floor Why rejected The framework cannot safely determine when advancing the offset is safe Consider the S3 Sink Connector Records 0 49 delivered to sink 50 100 filteredS3 Sink buffers records 0 49 hasn t flushed to S3 yetpreCommit returns quot not ready to commit quot Framework floor would commit offset 101S3 flush later fails records 0 49 permanently lostThe fundamental problem the framework doesn t know the sink s internal state The sink s preCommit return value is a deliberate signal about what s safe to commit not an oversight Any framework level override risks data loss for connectors with complex flush commit semantics Even a quot smart quot floor that only advances for partitions where the sink received no records can fail in edge cases A connector might use preCommit as a global quot hold everything quot signal across all partitionsA connector might have cross partition transactional semanticsA connector might coordinate offset commits with an external system s transactionThe notification approach is strictly safer it gives the sink complete information and lets it make the decision eliminating all framework side risk Alternative 2 Separate Callbacks per Skip ReasonApproach Two separate methods onFilteredRecord TopicPartition long for transform drops and onDlqRecord TopicPartition long for DLQ diversions Why rejected Same offset tracking logic From the sink s perspective both cases have identical offset management needs Two callbacks means duplicated logic in every connector implementation API surface One method with an enum parameter is cleaner than two methods doing the same thing Extensibility If new skip reasons are added in the future e g record size limits schema validation a new enum value is backward compatible a new method is not Precedent The SkipReason enum allows sinks that DO care about the distinction to branch on it Alternative 3 Enriching the preCommit ParameterApproach Change the preCommit Map lt TopicPartition OffsetAndMetadata gt signature to include metadata about which offsets correspond to skipped records For example preCommit Map lt TopicPartition OffsetAndMetadata gt Map lt TopicPartition List lt Long gt gt skippedOffsets Why rejected Breaks backward compatibility Changing preCommit signature is a source incompatible change All existing connectors would need to update Overloading Adding an overload with extra parameters is confusing and hard to deprecate Wrong abstraction preCommit is about committing skip notification is about record level awareness Mixing them creates an API that s hard to reason about Timing Skip information is available during conversion in convertMessages but preCommit is called much later The sink should learn about skips as they happen not retroactively Alternative 4 Automatic Offset Advancement with ConfigurationApproach Add a connector config transforms offset commit policy framework connector that controls whether the framework automatically commits offsets for skipped records Why rejected as a standalone solution Data loss risk Even with careful case analysis see Alternative 1 the framework cannot guarantee safety for all sink implementations A configuration option that enables data loss prone behavior shifts blame to operators Complexity Requires the framework to track filteredOffsets lastDeliveredOffsets and implement multi case floor logic This complexity is unnecessary if the sink is simply informed Still needs notification Even with this config connectors that want correct behavior with policy connector need the notification API anyway So this alternative is additive not a replacement However this could be reconsidered as a future enhancement layered on top of the notification API specifically for the narrow case where all records for a partition are filtered and the sink has no data at risk Alternative 5 SinkTaskContext ExtensionApproach Add a method to SinkTaskContext e g context skippedOffsets that the sink can query during preCommit to discover which offsets were skipped Why rejected Polling vs notification Forces the sink to remember to check during preCommit Easy to forget easy to get wrong A callback is harder to miss in code review State management ambiguity When does skippedOffsets reset After preCommit After commit succeeds The lifecycle is unclear Same information worse ergonomics The notification approach pushes information to the sink at the right time The context approach requires the sink to pull it at the right time Alternative 6 Per Transform Latency MetricsApproach Adding transform record latency avg and transform record latency max per transform Why rejected While useful for identifying slow transforms it was deferred to keep this KIP focused on record counting and the offset gap fix Latency metrics can be added in a follow up KIP using the same infrastructure adding Avg and Maxstats to the same MetricGroup instances Alternative 7 Separate Metric Group for Transform Operational MetricsApproach Creating a new connector transform operation metrics group separate from the existing connector transform metricsmetadata group Why rejected Fragments the JMX namespace operators would need to look in two placesThe existing group already has per transform tags and cardinalityKafka s convention is to co locate all metrics for a component in one groupAlternative 8 Instrumenting Inside TransformationStageApproach Placing the metric recording inside TransformationStage apply instead of TransformationChain apply Why rejected TransformationStage doesn t have visibility into whether RetryWithToleranceOperator tolerates an error which also produces a null return The chain is the natural orchestration point that sees the final outcome of each stageAvoids coupling TransformationStage to the metrics frameworkAlternative 9 Implementing Metrics via the Monitorable InterfaceApproach Having individual Transformation implementations opt into metrics via the Monitorable interface Why rejected Requires every transform including third party to implement metricsCannot capture chain level semantics filtered vs error tolerated Inconsistent coverage built in transforms would have metrics third party would notThe chain level approach provides uniform coverage with zero transform code changes

MotivationKafka Streams window and session state stores are internally divided into time based segments each backed by a separate RocksDB instance The segment interval controls how wide each segment is in time Currently the segment interval for window and session stores is computed automatically as max retentionPeriod 2 60 000ms and is not configurable through the public API This creates two problems Changing retention requires a full state store restore Because the segment interval is derived from the retention period any change to retention also changes the segment boundaries Since segment boundaries determine the on disk directory structure and key layout a retention change invalidates the existing state store data and requires restoring from the changelog topic This is unnecessarily disruptive a user who simply wants to keep data longer or shorter should not have to pay the cost of a full restore The default segment size is suboptimal for common access patterns Many streaming applications need a long retention or grace period e g 7 days but access recent data the vast majority of the time With the current formula a 7 day retention produces segments of 3 5 days This means the active segment the one receiving all writes and most reads is very large leading to heavier RocksDB compaction and lower cache hit ratios A user who knows their access pattern could benefit from smaller segments e g 1 hour keeping the active segment compact while still retaining historical data across many smaller segments Notably Stores persistentVersionedKeyValueStore already accepts an optional segmentInterval parameter introduced in KIP 889 Versioned State Stores KIP 889 established both the API pattern and the rationale for user configurable segments This KIP extends the same capability to window and session stores where the internal plumbing already supports a configurable segment interval it is simply not exposed in the public API Public InterfacesNew method overloads in org apache kafka streams state Stores Window storesjava CDATA public static WindowBytesStoreSupplier persistentWindowStore final String name final Duration retentionPeriod final Duration windowSize final boolean retainDuplicates final Duration segmentInterval throws IllegalArgumentException public static WindowBytesStoreSupplier persistentTimestampedWindowStore final String name final Duration retentionPeriod final Duration windowSize final boolean retainDuplicates final Duration segmentInterval throws IllegalArgumentException public static WindowBytesStoreSupplier persistentTimestampedWindowStoreWithHeaders final String name final Duration retentionPeriod final Duration windowSize final boolean retainDuplicates final Duration segmentInterval throws IllegalArgumentException Session storesjava CDATA public static SessionBytesStoreSupplier persistentSessionStore final String name final Duration retentionPeriod final Duration segmentInterval public static SessionBytesStoreSupplier persistentSessionStoreWithHeaders final String name final Duration retentionPeriod final Duration segmentInterval ValidationThe following constraints are enforced on segmentInterval Must be at least 60 000 milliseconds 1 minute This matches the minimum already used by the default formula max retentionPeriod 2 60 000ms Segments smaller than 1 minute would create an excessive number of RocksDB instances for any practical retention period For window stores must be greater than or equal to windowSize A segment smaller than the window size would cause a single window s data to span multiple RocksDB segments degrading read performance An IllegalArgumentException is thrown if these constraints are violated Javadoc for segmentInterval The only added parameter is segmentInterval The Javadoc is adapted from the existing Stores persistentVersionedKeyValueStore parameterjava CDATA param segmentInterval size of segments for storing records must be at least 60 seconds and for window stores must be at least as large as code windowSize Records within the same segment are stored updated and accessed together The only impact of this parameter is performance If segments are large and a workload results in many records being collected in a single segment performance may degrade as a result On the other hand reads that access older segments and out of order writes may slow down if there are too many segments For the new overloads the existing note about retentionPeriod is replaced by a note about segmentInterval since changing retentionPeriod alone no longer impacts the underlying storage format when segmentInterval is set explicitly java CDATA Note that it is not safe to change the value of segmentInterval between application restarts without clearing local state from application instances as this may cause incorrect values to be read from the state store otherwise Proposed ChangesThe changes are minimal because the internal plumbing already supports a configurable segment interval Stores java Add the new overloads listed above Each delegates to the existing private persistentWindowStore method or equivalent passing the user provided segmentInterval instead of the computed default Add validation as specified RocksDbSessionBytesStoreSupplier java add a constructor overload that accepts an explicit segmentInterval and adapt segmentIntervalMs to return the segmentInterval setNo changes needed to WindowBytesStoreSupplier interface already defines segmentIntervalMs SessionBytesStoreSupplier interface already defines segmentIntervalMs RocksDbWindowBytesStoreSupplier already accepts segmentInterval in its constructorAbstractSegments CachingWindowStore WindowStoreBuilder already consume segmentIntervalMs from the supplier No modifications required BuiltInDslStoreSuppliers the DSL path creates stores via Stores or internal supplier constructors and does not need to expose segment interval it is a low level tuning parameter not a DSL level concern Users who want to set it use Materialized as WindowBytesStoreSupplier with a custom supplier Compatibility Deprecation and Migration PlanBackward compatible All existing methods retain their current signatures and behavior The new overloads are purely additive No deprecationsMigration Users who currently instantiate internal suppliers directly e g new RocksDbWindowBytesStoreSupplier to control segment interval can migrate to the new public API overloads State store compatibility As noted in the Javadoc changing the segment interval for an existing store requires clearing local state since it changes the on disk segment layout This is the same constraint that already applies when retention changes today the difference is that with this KIP users can change retention without triggering a segment layout change Test PlanUnit tests for each new Stores overload verifying Correct segment interval is passed through to the underlying supplier Validation rejects invalid values below 60 seconds smaller than window size for window stores Default behavior is preserved when using the existing overloads without segmentInterval Integration tests verifying that a window session store created with a custom segment interval functions correctly put get range queries expiration cleanup Test that changing retention without changing segment interval does not require a state store restore the primary motivating use case Rejected AlternativesNA

discussions get unwieldy fast MotivationMessage types in Kafka are keyed by a unique apiKey to uniquely identify them These include all RPC types used by the brokers and controllers metadata records stored in the KRaft metadata log and the data stored by coordinators Kafka contributors regularly introduce new message types in order to evolve the Kafka protocol However contributors run the risk of adopting an apiKey that is subsequently claimed by another proposal while they prototype their work This is a problem shared by other Apache projects as well 0 A workaround for this is for contributors to use a large value for apiKey which is currently unused and is unlikely to be used in the near future apiKey is represented as a short with non negative range from 0 32767 This KIP proposes formalising the reservation of the last 1024 values i e 31744 32767 for private use ensuring future protocol changes would take the reserved values into account Public MotivationThe Apache Kafka clients are often wrapped by frameworks such as Spring Kafka does this itself in Kafka Streams and Kafka Connect There is no architected way of identifying clients running within such frameworks which can hinder problem determination When diagnosing an issue from the client logs the application code is not directly calling the Kafka client This means there s a mismatch between what the application developer wrote and how the Kafka client is being used Behaviors such as retries or transactions can be implemented in the framework rather than the application Having the information about whether a framework is being used can illuminate why the application is appearing to behave in a particular way Proposed ChangesThree client configurations are added which can be set by frameworks embedding Kafka clients producer consumer and admin The configurations are client framework name the name of the framework client framework version the version of the framework and client framework ID additional framework specific context which may not be relevant to all frameworks These are flowed to the broker in the ApiVersions request alongside the client software name and version providing more comprehensive context information about clients wrapped by frameworks The values are set using the CommonClientConfigs CLIENT FRAMEWORK NAME CONFIG CommonClientConfigs CLIENT FRAMEWORK VERSION CONFIG and CommonClientConfigs CLIENT FRAMEWORK ID CONFIG keys in the usual way These configs are not intended to be set by regular applications If a framework provides a way for the application to set its own Kafka configs the framework s own values for the client framework name version and ID take precedence over the values the application sets for these configs they are provided to be used by a framework The framework name should begin with the reversed Internet domain name for the framework owner followed by the framework s name For a framework such as Spring the framework name would be chosen by Spring and the framework version would reflect the version of Spring For Kafka s own frameworks Kafka Streams and Kafka Connect Apache Kafka automatically sets the 1071 https cwiki apache org confluence pages viewpage action pageId 393677857 introduced Streams groups the StreamsGroupDescribe API and the kafka streams groups sh command line tool The member IDs to application instances and for diagnosing static membership issues The rack ID is primarily useful when investigating rack aware task placement Since it is optional and is generally the regular member output information available in the regular output including the instance ID is not omitted when verbose output is requested Public InterfacesThis KIP introduces no new command line 446071036|This document contains some rough design notes about how to support transactional acknowledgements for share groups Application programming interfacePrior to KIP 1289 applications chose how to acknowledge record delivery using the share acknowledgement mode consumer configuration It seems to me that neither implicit nor explicit is really ideal I propose that we introduce a third acknowledgement mode transactional This gives a nice clean way to enforce correct API usage in the application Transactional acknowledgement mode has the following features Acknowledgements are explicit meaning that every record received from poll Duration must be acknowledged using ShareConsumer acknowledge before the next call to poll Duration ShareConsumer commitSync and ShareConsumer commitAsync are not permitted The acknowledgements are committed as part of a transaction so these specific methods are not appropriate ShareConsumer setAcknowledgementCommitCallback is likewise not permitted The acknowledgements will be completed once the transaction commits so the callback is not as useful as it is with asynchronous non transactional acknowledgements AcknowledgeMode RENEW is not permitted It is incompatible with transactions The following code snippet shows how the application code might look java CDATA producerProps put ProducerConfig TRANSACTIONAL ID CONFIG T1 consumerProps put ConsumerConfig GROUP ID CONFIG SG1 consumerProps put ConsumerConfig SHARE ACKNOWLEDGEMENT MODE CONFIG transactional try Producer producer new KafkaProducer prodProps ShareConsumer commitTransaction We need to define some kind of bridge between the producer and the share consumer so that shareConsumer acknowledge rec results in a transactional request to be sent to the share partition leader This is the purpose of producer setShareGroupTransactionAdapter The internal details need to be ironed out but this gives quite clean application code there s no Producer sendShareGroupAcknowledgementsToTransaction or equivalent for example Kafka protocolTo fit in with the current protocol design I think we need 2 or perhaps 3 depending on taste new RPCs They are that needs Flink Kafka Spark and Iceberg must either drive each engine control plane directly or connect to a sprawl of independent mostly read only MCP servers each with its own security posture no shared audit and no unified policy An MCP server that can reach a control plane a JobManager REST API a Kafka AdminClient a SQL gateway an Iceberg catalog is a privileged client Shipping one safely is effectively shipping an access control product authentication authorization approval for destructive actions redaction of secrets and personal data rate and cost limits and forensic audit Many existing options lack these controls and carry single maintainer sustainability risk A single governed gateway developed in the open under neutral governance gives the ecosystem a shared standard for how agents operate Apache systems safely RationaleA single governed gateway resolves the problems of the decentralized approach Security One place enforces identity authorization approval redaction egress and audit instead of each server reimplementing or omitting them Maintainability Adding an engine is a small adapter not a new security model There is one chain to review and harden so the security review surface stays flat as engines are added Governance One control plane for policy budget and provenance with a stable deny taxonomy so operators can alert on codes such as POLICY DENIED or APPROVAL REQUIRED across every engine with one rule Doing this under Apache governance keeps it neutral across vendors and engines rather than leaving agent access to fragmented single vendor 449286526|StatusCurrent state Under DiscussionDiscussion thread here Change the link from the KIP proposal email archive to your own email thread JIRA herePlease keep the discussion on the mailing list rather than commenting on the wiki wiki discussions get unwieldy fast MotivationKafka currently accepts any min insync replicas value of 1 or more with no relation to the replication factor of the topics it applies to A topic can be created with replication factor 1 config min insync replicas 2 and the request succeeds even though the configuration is contradictory the topic can never have enough in sync replicas to satisfy the configured minimum This misconfiguration is not hypothetical It has been reported since 2017 KAFKA 4680 where producing with acks all to such a topic fails with the retriable NotEnoughReplicasException retries that can never succeed and the resulting error log flood filled a broker s disk in a production cluster Replication tooling that creates topics on a destination cluster whose default min insync replicas exceeds the source topic s replication factor hits the same trap and the failure surfaces far from its cause KIP 966 Eligible Leader Replicas has already settled the semantic question the effective minimum ISR of a partition is defined as min min insync replicas replication factor and both the controller and the broker silently clamp to that value ReplicationControlManager getTopicEffectiveMinIsr Partition effectiveMinIsr In other words a min insync replicas above the replication factor already has no effect the configured value is simply ignored beyond the clamp Accepting a value the cluster will never honor is a silent footgun the user believes they have configured a durability guarantee that does not exist This KIP proposes to reject such configurations at the API boundary where the mistake is made topic creation and topic level configuration changes Public InterfacesNo new configurations request response schema fields error codes or APIs are introduced The change is new validation behavior on two existing request types using the existing INVALID CONFIG 40 error code APIScenarioCurrent behaviorProposed behaviorCreateTopicsThe topic s resolved replication factor is lower than its effective min insync replicasTopic is created the configured min ISR is silently clamped to the replication factorRequest fails with INVALID CONFIGIncrementalAlterConfigs AlterConfigs TOPIC resource min insync replicas is set to a value higher than the topic s replication factorChange is accepted and silently clampedRequest fails with INVALID CONFIGCreatePartitions AlterPartitionReassignments broker cluster and controller level configuration changesn an aUnchanged see Proposed Changes for rationale For CreateTopics the resolved replication factor is the request s value the size of the manual replica assignment if one is given or the cluster default default replication factor when the request passes 1 The effective min insync replicas is the value that would govern the new topic the topic level override in the request if present otherwise the cluster level dynamic default otherwise the static broker controller configuration Example error messages CDATA CreateTopics The topic s min insync replicas 3 must not exceed its replication factor 1 AlterConfigs Cannot set min insync replicas to 3 which exceeds the replication factor 1 of topic foo Proposed ChangesValidation at topic creationIn the KRaft controller ReplicationControlManager createTopic after the replication factor has been resolved from the request the manual assignment or the cluster default and before any records are generated the controller computes the effective min insync replicas for the new topic and rejects the creation with INVALID CONFIG if it exceeds the replication factor The check must live here rather than in the existing topic config validation path ControllerConfigurationValidator LogConfig validate because that path runs before the replication factor is resolved and receives only the topic name the replication factor is structurally unavailable to it Internal topics consumer offsets transaction state the share group and remote log metadata state topics are created through the same path and are validated identically A rejection there can only occur when the broker s own settings are contradictory e g offsets topic replication factor below the cluster s min insync replicas failing the creation with a clear message surfaces that operator misconfiguration instead of leaving an internal topic that cannot accept acks all writes Internal topic creation is retried by brokers so fixing the configuration heals the cluster without manual intervention Validation at topic level configuration changesIn the controller s configuration handling ConfigurationControlManager alongside the ELR related min insync replicas checks introduced by KIP 966 a SET or legacy alter of min insync replicas on a TOPIC resource is rejected with INVALID CONFIG when the new value exceeds the topic s current replication factor Both IncrementalAlterConfigs and the deprecated AlterConfigs funnel through the same validation and are covered A DELETE of a topic level min insync replicas override remains allowed even when the topic then falls back to a cluster level or static default that exceeds its replication factor The fallback value is not chosen by the caller and rejecting the delete would prevent returning a topic to defaults a topic in that state is governed by the effective min ISR clamp like other grandfathered configurations APPEND and SUBTRACT do not arise since min insync replicas is not a list type config What is deliberately not validatedExisting topics are grandfathered No existing topic is touched invalidated or mutated by this KIP Topics that already carry min insync replicas above their replication factor continue to work exactly as today governed by the KIP 966 clamp Only new requests that would create or change into a contradictory state are rejected Deletes of topic level min insync replicas overrides which fall back to a default that may exceed the replication factor See quot Validation at topic level configuration changes quot above for the rationale Cluster level min insync replicas changes Raising the cluster wide default may put existing low replication topics above the threshold but validating it would require scanning every topic on the controller and would block a legitimate operation hardening the default for future topics Existing topics remain protected by the clamp the recommended operator workflow is unchanged Partition reassignments that lower the replication factor below a topic s min insync replicas Reassignment is an operator driven surface with its own safeguard allowReplicationFactorChange KIP 860 and the clamp keeps the partition writable throughout Extending validation there can be a follow up if the community wants it Upgrade behaviorThe validation is request time logic on the active controller and requires no new metadata records so it is not gated on a metadata version or feature flag In a cluster with mixed controller versions during a rolling upgrade enforcement begins when an upgraded controller becomes active Compatibility Deprecation and Migration PlanThis is a backward incompatible behavior change by design requests that previously succeeded and produced a configuration the cluster silently ignores will now fail We believe the break is acceptable because The rejected configurations have no effect today since KIP 966 the effective min ISR is clamped to the replication factor no working setup can depend on the accepted but ignored value The failure is immediate at the API call that introduces the contradiction with a message naming both values as opposed to today s failure modes producer retry storms silent clamping that surface later and elsewhere There is precedent for tightening configuration constraints in a major minor release when the old values were harmful e g KIP 1030 One workflow requires reordering increasing durability on an existing topic by setting min insync replicas above the current replication factor before adding replicas After this KIP the replication factor must be increased first via reassignment then min insync replicas Topic creation workflows are unaffected as long as the requested configuration is self consistent Known deployment patterns affected Kafka Connect accepts topic level settings for its internal topics for example config storage min insync replicas together with config storage replication factor 1 to use the broker default likewise for the offset and status topics and for source connector auto created topics via topic creation lt alias gt Where the resulting min insync replicas exceeds the resolved replication factor internal topic creation now fails at worker startup with an explicit error instead of silently creating a topic with a weaker guarantee than the one requested The remedy is to make the two settings consistent MirrorMaker 2 is unaffected in its default configuration min insync replicas is on the default config properties exclude list and is not synced to mirror topics Deployments that override the exclude list to sync min insync replicas can hit the new validation when the source topic s value exceeds the mirror topic s replication factor No deprecation or migration tooling is needed nothing is removed and existing topics including already contradictory ones are untouched Lowering a topic s replication factor is not blocked so any grandfathered topic can still be repaired in either direction raise RF or lower min ISR Test PlanUnit tests in ReplicationControlManagerTest and ConfigurationControlManagerTest covering creation with explicit defaulted and manually assigned replication factors against topic level cluster level and static min ISR sources topic level alteration above at below the replication factor and legacy AlterConfigs The existing test asserting that a topic with min insync replicas above its replication factor is accepted testEligibleLeaderReplicas EffectiveMinIsr will be updated accordingly Integration coverage is added to the existing CreateTopics AlterConfigs admin client tests Documentation PlanThe min insync replicas description in the topic and broker configuration reference will state the new constraint and the release s upgrade notes will call out the behavior change Rejected AlternativesThrow a new non retriable exception at produce time KIP 579 s approach This was the direction proposed in 2020 for KAFKA 4680 keep the configuration legal but fail acks all produces with a dedicated InconsistentReplicaConfigurationException It only fires once the data path is exercised the misconfiguration is accepted and discovered later by a different principal than the one who made it It also predates KIP 966 which has since made the configuration semantically void rather than quot legal but dangerous quot Rejecting at configuration time is strictly earlier and clearer KIP 579 itself rejected configuration time validation partly because such topics were usable with acks all the KIP 966 clamp has since removed any behavior that depended on the un clamped value which is why this KIP revisits that conclusion Introduce a new error code KIP 579 had reserved INCONSISTENT REPLICA CONFIGURATION 89 that code has since been assigned to THROTTLING QUOTA EXCEEDED Clients that don t know a new code surface it as UnknownServerException INVALID CONFIG is already returned by both affected APIs for other invalid topic configurations is handled by every client version and describes the problem accurately Validate cluster level min insync replicas changes against all existing topics Requires an O topics scan on the controller for a dynamic config update and would block hardening the default for future topics just because legacy low replication topics exist The clamp already protects existing topics Rely on CreateTopicPolicy AlterConfigPolicy KIP 108 KIP 133 Operators can enforce this today with a custom policy but policies are opt in must be deployed on every cluster and don t help the users who hit this by accident which is exactly the population this KIP is for A contradiction between two settings of the same topic is a consistency rule not a site policy Documentation only fix The constraint has been documented in the min insync replicas description for years KAFKA 4680 style incidents kept occurring regardless

MotivationBrokers already expose per client quota usage byte rate request time and throttle time throttle time They do not expose how that usage compares to the effective quota applied to the same quota sensor That join is left to operators scrape the rate then independently resolve user client id and default overrides or a custom ClientQuotaCallback from a different path Limits can differ by orders of magnitude and can change dynamically so absolute rate alerts do not transfer across clients throttle time only changes after throttling has occurred Operators need a normalized rate signal that identifies clients whose recent usage is approaching or exceeding the quota actually applied on that broker without requiring the monitoring stack to resolve the quota independently KIP 1257 Partition Size Percentage Metrics for Storage Monitoring established the precedent of shipping a normalized percentage from Kafka rather than requiring operators to compute it externally The analogy is only partial retention bytes is a topic configuration while client quotas are resolved per quota entity through the existing quota hierarchy and optional callbacks This KIP preserves the existing quota resolution and enforcement behavior Proposed ChangesAdd quota utilization as an additional attribute on the existing client quota MBeans No new MBean type ObjectName sensor or quota entity is windowed mutation rate ratio would therefore not represent how much of the resource that actually controls throttling is currently available For example a burst can exhaust tokens and cause throttle time while the windowed mutation rate is still below 100 Conversely the windowed mutation rate can remain above 100 after the token bucket has begun to refill A future KIP can define an appropriate implementations to earlier Java versions Note that the SSLParameters setNamedGroups API is available from Java 20 but the PQC named groups themselves e g x25519 mlkem768 require Java 27 or a vendor backport that includes JEP 527 Due to threats like quot harvest now decrypt later quot many organizations are now actively considering PQC TLS It is also mandated by several governments and industries MotivationRack aware assignment is costly and in the common case changes nothing Yet the group coordinator pays for it for every group Rack aware assignment gives each member partitions with a replica in its rack so that the member can fetch from that replica instead of crossing racks KIP 392 It changes nothing in two common cases Fetch from follower is not used so the members fetch from the leader It is off by default for consumers and share consumers do not support it The replicas of every partition already cover all racks as with three availability zones and a replication factor of three Neither the coordinator nor the assignor can tell which case applies without doing the work that would be wasted The assignor Rack awareness is planned for the built in consumer assignors KAFKA 19387 A rack aware assignor has to read the racks of the replicas of every subscribed partition on every assignment Finding out whether the racks matter costs as much as using them So every consumer group would pay this cost on every assignment including in the two cases above The metadata hash The coordinator already pays for the racks today Since KIP 1101 the metadata hash of every group covers the racks of the replicas of every subscribed partition Computing it looks up the rack of every replica and it is recomputed after every change to a subscribed topic including leader and ISR changes A rack change also bumps the group epoch even though no built in assignor uses racks today The classic protocol makes rack awareness opt in a consumer only considers racks when client rack is set KIP 881 This KIP does the same on the server for consumer groups with a broker configuration that is off by default Share and streams groups cannot use the racks today so they stop paying for them Public consumer groups When enabled the assignor is given the rack ids of the members and the racks of the partition replicas and a change of the racks of a subscribed partition triggers a new assignment It is only useful when both of the following hold the consumers use fetch from follower replica selector class on the brokers and client rack on the consumers and the partitions do not have a replica in every rack or availability zone Otherwise rack aware assignment changes nothing and only adds cost Assignor interfaceA new default method on org apache kafka coordinator group api assignor GroupSpec condition now largestRecordTimestamp gt local retention ms succeeds The age is measured from record timestamps which producers set This causes two problems 1 Old timestampsFor records produced with timestamps older than local retention ms the local copy is deleted as soon as the segment is uploaded to remote storage The configured local window is zero for this data for example during backfills or replays Example local retention ms is 1 hour At 10 00 a backfill writes records stamped 07 00 the same day The segment is uploaded at 10 05 At the next retention check the records are already about 3 hours old so the local copy is deleted right away Consumers reading this data in the next hour must fetch it from remote storage 2 Future timestampsRecords produced with future timestamps would block deletion such a segment can t be deleted by time until its timestamp plus local retention ms has passed and it blocks deletion of every later segment KAFKA 20609 works around this by using the segment file s last modified time instead But a disk replacement or a partition move resets that time so the segment s age restarts from zero and its deletion is delayed again Example With local retention ms 1 hour a segment uploaded at 10 05 is deleted locally around 11 05 whatever timestamps its records have This KIP changes local retention ms and log local retention ms for tiered topics to 451979367|Expose Explicit Configuration Deletions to AlterConfigPolicyStatusCurrent state Under DiscussionDiscussion thread TBDJIRA KAFKA 21147Released TBDMotivationAlterConfigPolicy implementations receive an AlterConfigPolicy RequestMetadata instance when a configuration change is validated Its configs method does not consistently identify explicit DELETE operations made through the Incremental Alter Configs API For a topic configuration deleting an unset override is a no op and does not generate a ConfigRecord Consequently the key is absent from configs For a broker configuration Kafka generates a record even when the configuration is unset so the key is present in configs with a null value A policy therefore cannot reliably determine whether a key was explicitly deleted by inspecting configs Changing configs so every explicit deletion appears as a key mapped to null would resolve this inconsistency but it would also change the behavior observed by existing policy implementations In particular KIP 1252 introduced alter config policy kraft compatibility enable in Kafka 3 9 2 so ZooKeeper based clusters could opt into the existing KRaft policy behavior before migrating Changing that KRaft behavior in a later release would undermine the compatibility guarantee for users who enabled the setting This KIP proposes an additive API that exposes explicit deletions consistently while preserving the existing configs contract and behavior Existing policies continue to receive the same map while policies that need operation level deletion information can opt into the new method Public InterfacesThis KIP adds the following constructor and methods to the public AlterConfigPolicy RequestMetadata class public RequestMetadata ConfigResource resource Map lt String String gt configs Set lt String gt deletedConfigs public Set lt String gt deletedConfigs public Map lt String String gt configsWithoutNullValues The existing constructor remains unchanged public RequestMetadata ConfigResource resource Map lt String String gt configs Instances created with the existing constructor return an empty set from deletedConfigs deletedConfigs deletedConfigs returns the names of configurations explicitly targeted by DELETE operations in an Incremental Alter Configs request It includes deletions that do not generate metadata records such as deleting an unset topic configuration The returned set is empty for legacy Alter Configs requests It does not include configurations implicitly removed because they were omitted from a legacy full replacement request The returned set is immutable and does not contain null configsWithoutNullValues configsWithoutNullValues returns the entries from configs whose values are non null This gives policy implementations a direct way to consume the existing configuration representation without interpreting null as either a value or an operation Calling this method does not change the meaning of configs and does not replace deletedConfigs a no op topic deletion may be absent from both maps but will still be present in deletedConfigs Proposed ChangesWhen processing an Incremental Alter Configs request the controller will collect the key of every explicitly requested DELETE operation and pass those keys to RequestMetadata Collection is based on the request operations rather than generated metadata records so it is consistent across resource types and includes no op deletions The behavior visible to a policy will be RequestExisting configs New deletedConfigs New configsWithoutNullValues Incremental SETExisting behavior resulting key valueEmptySame non null entryIncremental APPEND or SUBTRACTExisting behavior resulting key valueEmptySame non null entryDelete an existing topic overrideExisting behavior key mapped to nullDeleted keyEntry omittedDelete an unset topic overrideExisting behavior key omittedDeleted keyEntry omittedDelete a broker configurationExisting behavior key mapped to null when a record is generatedDeleted keyEntry omittedLegacy Alter Configs requestExisting behaviorEmptyNon null entries from configs The existing two argument constructor will delegate to the new constructor with an empty deletion set To avoid changing behavior unrelated to the new accessors configs resource equals Object hashCode and toString retain their existing semantics In particular the new deletion set will not alter equality or hash code results for otherwise equivalent RequestMetadata instances No protocol configuration command line metric or metadata record changes are introduced Compatibility Deprecation and Migration PlanThe change is binary and source compatible for existing AlterConfigPolicy implementations Existing implementations do not need to be rebuilt or modified configs retains its current contents for every request This preserves the KRaft behavior used as the compatibility target by KIP 1252 and avoids surprising users migrating from Kafka 3 9 2 with alter config policy kraft compatibility enable true Policies that need to validate explicit deletions can adopt deletedConfigs Policies that currently filter null values from configs can optionally adopt configsWithoutNullValues There is no deprecation and no migration tool is required Test PlanUnit tests will verify that deleting an unset topic configuration leaves configs unchanged and exposes the key through deletedConfigs deleting an existing topic configuration exposes the key through deletedConfigs while preserving the existing null entry in configs deleting an unset broker configuration exposes the key through deletedConfigs while preserving existing configs behavior non delete incremental operations do not populate deletedConfigs legacy Alter Configs requests return an empty deletion set configsWithoutNullValues excludes null valued entries without changing configs the existing constructor continues to produce metadata with an empty deletion set andequality and hash code behavior remain compatible with existing RequestMetadata instances No new system test is required because this proposal changes only the in process arguments passed by the controller to the configured policy Existing controller and policy unit tests exercise that boundary directly Documentation PlanThe Javadocs for RequestMetadata configs will document its existing record derived behavior including the differing representation of no op topic deletions and broker deletions The new constructor and accessors will document the explicit deletion semantics and the behavior of legacy Alter Configs requests No user facing broker configuration documentation changes are required Rejected AlternativesChange configs to include every explicit deletion as a null valueThis was the approach taken by the original fix for KAFKA 19028 It is simple and makes topic and broker deletion behavior consistent inside the existing map It also directly addresses the correctness concern that policies should be able to recognize every requested deletion However it changes the input observed by existing policies Users who enabled the KIP 1252 compatibility setting before migrating from ZooKeeper mode would no longer receive the KRaft behavior they explicitly selected Because policy implementations may reject requests based on map membership or null values the change could alter request outcomes after an upgrade The additive API achieves the same validation capability without imposing that behavior change on existing policies Return effective values after deletions from configs Returning the default or inherited value after a deletion could make configs look consistent with the effective state representation used for some other incremental operations It would not communicate that a deletion was explicitly requested and a policy could not distinguish deletion from setting the same effective value It would also change existing behavior Add only deletedConfigs This is sufficient to identify explicit deletions Adding configsWithoutNullValues as well provides an unambiguous non null view for policies and avoids requiring every implementation to duplicate filtering logic The two methods have distinct roles one reports the requested operation while the other provides a value only view of the existing map Replace AlterConfigPolicy with a new policy interfaceA new interface could model each incremental operation explicitly and address broader limitations of the existing policy API That is substantially larger than the problem tracked by KAFKA 21147 would require a migration and deprecation plan and would delay a narrowly scoped way to validate explicit deletions Such a redesign can be proposed independently if broader policy requirements justify it 
451979375|Allow Brokers to Disable Compression Types for Client WritesStatusCurrent state Under DiscussionDiscussion thread TBDJIRA KAFKA 21178Released TBDPlease keep the discussion on the mailing list rather than commenting on the wiki MotivationKafka supports gzip Snappy LZ4 and Zstandard compression for record batches Brokers must retain support for decompressing every codec that may be present in existing log segments Removing a codec implementation from Kafka would therefore prevent brokers from reading historical records that use that codec At the same time operators may need to prevent new records from being written with a particular compression type Reasons include a vulnerability in a compression library a codec implementation becoming unmaintained native library compatibility problems or an operational policy that prohibits a codec The existing compression type broker and topic configuration does not provide this protection When it is set to a specific codec Kafka recompresses incoming records using that codec However Kafka must first decompress a producer supplied batch Consequently forcing a different final compression type does not prevent a client from sending records encoded with an undesired codec This KIP proposes a broker controlled denylist for compression types used by new client writes The broker will reject a write before decompressing its records when either The producer supplied a disabled compression type orThe broker would recompress the records using a disabled compression type The restriction will not apply when reading or replicating existing records This preserves compatibility with historical log data and allows replicas to remain synchronized Public InterfacesNew broker configurationA new broker configuration will be introduced PropertyValueNamecompression disabled typesTypeListDefaultEmpty listValid valuesgzip snappy lz4 zstdDynamic update modeCluster wideImportanceHighExample compression disabled types snappy lz4 The configuration contains a comma separated list of compression types that brokers must reject for new client writes An empty list preserves the existing behavior and permits every compression type supported by Kafka none is not a valid entry because uncompressed records do not invoke an external compression implementation This is a broker only configuration It will not have a corresponding topic level configuration and therefore cannot be overridden by a topic configuration Produce API behaviorNo request or response schema changes are proposed When a client produce request uses a disabled compression type the affected partition will return the existing UNSUPPORTED COMPRESSION TYPE error The same error will be returned when the effective topic configuration would cause the broker to recompress the records using a disabled type For example given compression disabled types snappy the broker will reject both of the following cases A producer sends a Snappy compressed record batch regardless of the effective compression type The effective topic configuration has compression type snappy even when the producer sends an uncompressed batch or uses another compression type Other partitions in the same produce request will continue to be processed according to the existing produce request behavior Dynamic configurationcompression disabled types will support cluster wide dynamic updates through the existing broker configuration API For example bin kafka configs sh bootstrap server localhost 9092 entity type brokers entity default alter add config compression disabled types snappy lz4A dynamic update will be propagated to existing logs without requiring a broker restart As with other dynamic broker configurations propagation is asynchronous During propagation brokers may temporarily observe different values Enforcement for a partition is determined by the current configuration of its leader Proposed ChangesConfiguration parsing and propagationThe broker configuration definition will declare compression disabled types as a list containing zero or more supported compressed record codecs Unknown values will cause configuration validation to fail For example compression disabled types brotli will be rejected because Brotli is not a Kafka record batch compression type The parsed configuration will be represented internally as a set of compression types It will be included in the broker s default log configuration and propagated to existing logs when the dynamic broker configuration changes The value will be stored as an internal log property rather than exposed as a topic property This prevents principals with topic configuration privileges from overriding a restriction established by the cluster administrator Produce path validationKafka currently determines two compression types while processing a client append The source compression type declared in the producer s record batch header The target compression type selected from the effective compression type configuration For client originated appends Kafka will check both types against compression disabled types before record validation or decompression begins If either compression type is disabled Kafka will throw UnsupportedCompressionTypeException The existing exception to protocol mapping will return UNSUPPORTED COMPRESSION TYPE in the produce response Checking the producer compression type before decompression is important because it avoids invoking the disabled codec while processing the rejected request Checking the target compression type prevents Kafka itself from writing data with a disabled codec Append originsThe restriction will apply only to appends with CLIENT origin It will not apply to REPLICATION appendsCOORDINATOR appendsRAFT LEADER appendsReplication must remain permitted so that followers can receive records already accepted by a leader and historical partitions can be reassigned or recovered Coordinator and Raft writes are trusted broker internal operations and are not controlled by external producers Compression used by internal topics continues to be governed by the existing internal topic configurations Existing recordsThe proposed configuration does not disable decompression globally Existing records using a disabled compression type may still be Fetched by consumersReplicated between brokersRecovered during broker startupExamined by broker log operationsProcessed by log compactionThis distinction is required because Kafka cannot safely remove the ability to interpret codecs already present in log segments The configuration prevents additional client data using the codec from entering the log it is not a mechanism for removing or rewriting historical data Interaction with compression typeThe existing compression type setting continues to select the final on disk compression type If its effective value selects a codec included in compression disabled types new client writes will be rejected with UNSUPPORTED COMPRESSION TYPE For example compression type snappy compression disabled types snappy is a valid configuration but client writes governed by that effective compression configuration will be rejected This permits administrators to disable a codec dynamically even when existing topics or broker defaults still select it Administrators can subsequently change compression type without making the denylist update dependent on simultaneous topic configuration changes When compression type producer the producer s source compression type is also the target type and the same validation applies Compatibility Deprecation and Migration PlanThe default value is an empty list so upgrading Kafka will not change existing behavior No existing configuration API record format or compression type is deprecated or removed Operators who enable the configuration must ensure that producers stop using the disabled codecs Produce requests that continue to use them will fail with UNSUPPORTED COMPRESSION TYPE A suggested migration sequence is Identify producers using the codec that will be disabled Reconfigure those producers to use another codec or no compression Confirm that the new producer configuration has taken effect Add the codec to compression disabled types Monitor produce errors for clients that still use the disabled codec Before enabling the setting during a rolling upgrade every broker that may become a partition leader should run a Kafka version supporting this KIP Otherwise enforcement may depend on which broker is currently the leader Before downgrading to a version that does not support this KIP operators should remove the dynamic configuration Static configuration should also be removed from broker property files before starting an older broker version Disabling a codec does not rewrite existing segments Operators must retain the corresponding codec library while historical records using that codec remain in the cluster Test PlanUnit tests will verify that The default disabled type list is empty Every supported codec can be configured in the list Unknown compression types are rejected during configuration validation A producer batch using gzip Snappy LZ4 or Zstandard is rejected when its compression type is disabled An uncompressed producer batch is accepted when its type is not disabled A client write is rejected when the broker selected target compression type is disabled A replication append using a disabled compression type remains accepted Rejected records are not appended to the log Configuration tests will verify that The broker configuration is parsed correctly Dynamic updates are propagated through the broker and log configuration layers The setting is not exposed as an overridable topic configuration Integration tests will dynamically disable a codec and verify that A produce request using that codec succeeds before the update The same behavior is localized to broker configuration propagation and produce path validation which are covered by the integration tests Documentation PlanThe generated broker configuration reference will document The configuration name and defaultSupported compression typesDynamic update supportThe fact that it applies only to new client writesThe behavior of historical records and replicationIts interaction with compression typeThe broker configuration documentation will also include compression disabled types in the section describing dynamic configuration updates Rejected AlternativesRemove the affected codec implementationRemoving a codec implementation would make Kafka unable to read existing log segments using that codec This could prevent broker recovery replication consumer fetches and log maintenance Kafka must retain decompression support for historical data so removing a codec is not a viable mitigation Use compression type to force a different codecSetting compression type does not prevent clients from sending batches using another codec Kafka may need to decompress the producer batch before recompressing it with the configured target codec Therefore this does not protect the broker from processing an undesired producer supplied codec Introduce a topic level configurationA topic level configuration would allow a principal with topic configuration privileges to override the broker s restriction Codec disabling is an operator controlled broker policy and should apply consistently across client writable topics A broker only configuration also avoids requiring administrators to update every existing and newly created topic Use an allowlist instead of a denylistAn allowlist could provide stricter control but would require operators to enumerate every permitted codec It would also make the default and upgrade behavior more complicated when Kafka adds a new compression type A denylist preserves compatibility by default and directly supports the operational requirement to disable one or more problematic codecs Apply the restriction to replicationRejecting replicated records would cause followers to fall out of sync when the leader contains records using a disabled codec It would also interfere with partition reassignment and recovery of historical data The leader is responsible for enforcing the policy on new client writes Followers must continue accepting the resulting replicated log Disable decompression everywherePreventing all decompression of a disabled codec would affect consumer fetches log recovery compaction timestamp searches and other operations over historical data The proposal intentionally limits enforcement to new client writes so that existing data remains usable
